See also: completó and completò

English

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

completo (plural completos)

  1. (slang) A hot dog with the works.
  2. (baseball, slang) A complete game.

Asturian

[edit]

Adjective

[edit]

completo

  1. neuter of completu

Catalan

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): (Central) [kumˈplɛ.tu]
  • IPA(key): (Balearic) [komˈplɛ.to], [komˈple.to]
  • IPA(key): (Valencia) [komˈple.to]

Verb

[edit]

completo

  1. first-person singular present indicative of completar

Galician

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Learned borrowing from Latin completus.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /komˈplɛto/ [komˈplɛ.t̪ʊ]
  • Rhymes: -ɛto
  • Hyphenation: com‧ple‧to

Adjective

[edit]

completo (feminine completa, masculine plural completos, feminine plural completas)

  1. complete
  2. completed

Antonyms

[edit]
  • incompleto

Derived terms

[edit]
  • completamente

Further reading

[edit]
  • “completo”, in Dicionario da Real Academia Galega (in Galician), A Coruña: Royal Galician Academy, 2012–2026
  • “completo”, in Dicionário Estraviz de galego (in Galician), 2014–2026

Italian

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /komˈplɛ.to/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -ɛto
  • Hyphenation: com‧plè‧to

Etymology 1

[edit]

Borrowed from Latin completus.

Adjective

[edit]

completo (feminine completa, masculine plural completi, feminine plural complete)

  1. complete, entire, full, whole
    Synonym: intero
    Antonym: incompleto
  2. complete, absolute, total
    Synonyms: assoluto, totale
    Antonym: incompleto
Related terms
[edit]
  • compiere
  • complemento
  • completamente
  • completamento
  • completare
  • completezza
  • completivo

Noun

[edit]

completo m (plural completi)

  1. suit
  2. outfit
  3. set
  4. 2-piece set

Etymology 2

[edit]

Verb

[edit]

completo

  1. first-person singular present indicative of completare

Anagrams

[edit]
  • col tempo

Latin

[edit]

Verb

[edit]

complētō

  1. second/third-person singular future active imperative of compleō

Borrowed from Latin complētus.

Adjective

[edit]

completo (feminine completa, masculine plural completos, feminine plural completas)

  1. full, complete
  2. completed
Related terms
[edit]
  • complemento
  • completar
  • cumprir

Participle

[edit]

completo (short participle, feminine completa, masculine plural completos, feminine plural completas)

  1. past participle of completar

Etymology 2

[edit]

Verb

[edit]

completo

  1. first-person singular present indicative of completar

Spanish

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /komˈpleto/ [kõmˈple.t̪o]
  • Audio (Colombia):(file)
  • Rhymes: -eto
  • Syllabification: com‧ple‧to

Etymology 1

[edit]

Borrowed from Latin complētus. Doublet of cumplido.

Adjective

[edit]

completo (feminine completa, masculine plural completos, feminine plural completas, superlative completísimo)

  1. full, complete
    Synonyms: lleno, repleto
  2. completed
Derived terms
[edit]
  • a tiempo completo
  • al completo
  • completamente
  • completitud
  • concurso completo
  • de tiempo completo
  • nombre completo
  • pensión completa
Related terms
[edit]
  • complemento
  • completar
  • completivo
  • cumplir
  • repleto

Noun

[edit]

completo m (plural completos)

  1. (Chile) hot dog, usually served with chopped tomatoes, mayonnaise, and avocado paste or sauerkraut
    Synonym: perrito caliente
Derived terms
[edit]
  • papapleto
  • sushipleto
Descendants
[edit]
  • → Cebuano: kompleto
  • → Tagalog: kompleto

Etymology 2

[edit]

Verb

[edit]

completo

  1. first-person singular present indicative of completar
